description: #3830 — the two `property_definitions` WRITERS that answer with the row, driven through the command leg (`via: "command"`; neither appends an op, so the op log stays empty and `expected` carries only the seeded page). Pins `create_property_def`'s shape validation (bad value_type, bad key) and its INSERT OR IGNORE idempotency — a second create for the same key keeps the FIRST declaration, value_type and all — plus `update_property_def_options`' non-empty-JSON-array check, its select-type-only guard (the seeded text `note`) and its NotFound on an unknown key. Read back through the `list_property_defs` / `get_property_def` steps pinned by #4939. NOT pinned here: `conflicting_existing_values` (the #4399 probe that refuses a declaration which would orphan values the vault already holds under that key) — the mock has no equivalent, and the seed deliberately declares no `block_properties` row under either key. #4710 adds the `url` declaration and a value under it. Re-author `expected` / `expected_ops` / `expected_queries` via CONFORMANCE_UPDATE=1.
name: property_def_writes

ops.comment: The happy path: a select-type definition carries its options array through.
ops.name: create_select_def

ops.comment: INSERT OR IGNORE idempotency: the existing row wins, so the response is still the SELECT definition with its options — not the text one this op asked for.
ops.name: create_existing_def_keeps_first

ops.comment: validate_property_def_shape refuses a value_type outside text/number/date/select/ref/boolean/url.
ops.name: create_def_bad_value_type_rejects

ops.comment: #4710 — `url` is in the closed set (migration 0120). No options: a url is text with a link rendering.
ops.name: create_url_def

ops.comment: #4710 — under a `url` declaration the value lands in value_text, so the snapshot reads it back as Text. The engine refuses any other slot (`validate_property_value_url_with_number_payload_rejects`); the replay leg appends ops without that validator and `set_property` has no command-leg arm, so the refusal is pinned there rather than here.
The happy path: the widened array is read back from inside the tx.
ops.name: update_select_options

ops.comment: An empty array is refused before the row is touched, so priority_level keeps the three options above.
ops.name: update_options_empty_rejects

ops.comment: Options only mean something on a select-type definition; the seeded text `note` is refused.
ops.name: update_options_on_text_def_rejects

ops.comment: An unknown key is NotFound, not a validation refusal.
ops.name: update_options_unknown_key_rejects

ops.comment: #5057 — the command leg gained a unit-return shape in #5064, which is what this waiver said it was waiting for. A missing key is NotFound.
ops.name: delete_an_unknown_def_is_not_found

ops.comment: A built-in reserved key is not the user's to remove.
ops.name: delete_a_builtin_def_is_refused

ops.comment: S1 carries a `note` property, so the definition is still in use. Refused rather than orphaning the rows — this is why the seed grows one property.
ops.name: delete_a_def_with_live_rows_is_refused

ops.comment: The happy path: `priority_level` was created by an op above and nothing references it, so it goes. The `list_property_defs` step below is what observes the removal, since `property_definitions` is outside the snapshot.
ops.name: delete_an_unused_def

queries.comment: The whole registry after the ops: `note` survives (its delete was refused for the live row) and `priority_level` is gone.
queries.name: registry_after_writes

queries.comment: The point lookup on the definition the refusals left alone.
queries.name: note_after_writes
